authorization.why_the_cutover_is_not_authorized_here: these six answers open gates. They do not authorize the cutover steps themselves: §4.4 of the phase briefing orders the consumer swap and the blue shutdown, and each production-affecting step still waits for explicit approval at the time it is executed. Three of the six also require a physical action by the owner that no agent can perform.

revocation_ordering.condition: revoke claude-araripe-v2-staging-rw only AFTER a CI lane deposits runs (scripts/assemble_green_run.py apply) with the v2-staging identity — or with an explicit owner decision to stop depositing
revocation_ordering.the_condition_as_first_written: revoke after the site products are generated (docs/operations/PHASE_6_OWNER_DECISIONS_2026-09-17.md §D1)
revocation_ordering.why_that_was_too_early: measured 2026-09-18. Two separate findings. First, the site products do NOT need this credential at cutover: site/scripts/site_artifact.py reads the release through RouteReader, an HTTP GET with no credential, and site/.github/workflows/green_site_publish.yml references no R2 secret at all — so generating them was never the binding constraint. Second, D5 IS the binding constraint: the durable-history package adds a write to atomic_publish.promote and rollback, re-proving it end to end requires writing to araripe-v2-staging, the change lives on a feature branch until it merges, and all three backend Environments (v2-staging, v2-promotion, cloudflare-green-control) have a deployment branch policy of main only — confirmed by gh api on 2026-09-18. There is also no green deposit lane at all; GREEN_PROOFS_2026-09-07.md §(run assembly) records that the proof run was assembled and deposited with the LOCAL staging identity. So revoking before D5 would leave the re-proof executable only by merging unproven code to main first, which inverts the safety order the package exists to protect.
revocation_ordering.what_is_safe_to_revoke_before: nothing this phase needs until a CI deposit lane exists. Revocation stays the last step of D1; what changed is which step it waits for.
revocation_ordering.the_condition_as_corrected_on_2026_09_18: revoke claude-araripe-v2-staging-rw only AFTER the D5 durable promotion history is built and re-proven against real R2
revocation_ordering.why_the_2026_09_18_correction_was_also_w: measured 2026-09-27 in the code, not inferred. The local profile credential is opt-in per call site, and exactly two scripts opt in: scripts/assemble_green_run.py and scripts/stage_green_run.py — pinned by tests/test_profile_credential_fallback.py::test_only_the_two_lane_two_entry_points_opt_in. The promotion CLI, scripts/publish_green_release.py, which is what runs promote and rollback, REFUSES the fallback — test_every_build_client_call_in_the_promotion_cli_refuses_the_fallback. So the D5 change to promote/rollback can never be re-proven with the local credential: it is re-proven from main through the v2-promotion lanes (v2_operational_publish.yml, v2_promotion_lane.yml), exactly as the five proofs of 2026-09-07 were. D5 does not depend on the credential at all. My memory index already said 'credencial por profile é opt-in por call site' and I did not consult it.
revocation_ordering.what_actually_depends_on_the_local_crede: the DEPOSIT of a run prefix. scripts/assemble_green_run.py apply writes runs/<run-id>/ into araripe-v2-staging, and no workflow runs it — `git grep assemble_green_run .github/workflows/` on origin/main returns nothing. stage_green_run.py does run in CI (v2_operational_publish.yml, with R2_STAGING_*), but it is read-only validation. Revoking today would remove the only way to put a new run into the bucket, and the post-cutover scheduled process needs deposits twice a week.

ci_lane.met_when: a dispatch of v2_green_deposit_lane.yml from main deposits a runs/ci-<run_id>/ prefix and its own stage_green_run.py step validates it; the run id is then recorded here as proven_by_run and condition_met becomes true
ci_lane.proof: 2026-09-28, dispatched from main at the merge of #74: window 2026-08-25..2026-08-31 as araripe-green-detect; 4/4 terminal, ledger pl-v3-a54399279c38f3f194bfda10f865520ca5dfe226628719d1f57a71e65ea6358b; runs/ci-36432616599/ created 6 objects, run.json last; stage_green_run.py validated it read-only; the green pointer stayed at sequence 14. An earlier dispatch, 36432410617, failed at dependency install and wrote nothing.

the_third_local_caller.why_it_accepts_the_local_key: its upload subcommand puts baseline 2.1.0 (72 rasters, 13 GB, only ever on the owner's machine) into araripe-v2-staging once, and an operator must not export the secret to do it
the_third_local_caller.why_it_does_not_move_the_condition: the upload is ONE-TIME: after 72/72 objects exist the lane only fetches, with the v2-staging Environment identity. The local key is needed for nothing the lane does. If the upload were ever repeated it would be all `unchanged` (put_if_absent), and a different local copy is refused before any write
the_third_local_caller.upload_evidence: 2026-09-28: created 72, unchanged 0, conflict 0; the bucket lists 72 objects and 13626201392 bytes under baselines_v2/2.1.0/, equal to the manifest's byte sum (docs/implementation/PHASE_6F_2026-09-28.md §2)

before_revoking_also.what: the 2026 replay's final persistence state — 986744489 bytes, sha256 5eb17f838b35251b3748dbc26310918a8fa7a00ce99b4f3c501dd5887ac987ce, the value runs/rep-2026-08-30-v3/run.json declares — exists in ONE copy, in the replay's isolated directory on the owner's machine, and in no bucket

before_revoking_also.owner_guidance: do not revoke until the next package places the seed, or until the owner decides the seed will be regenerated in CI instead

d1_where_the_new_version_lives.why_not_option_b: measured 2026-09-17. Creating a final bucket and copying the release costs far more than the 1 778 202 736 bytes of the current release: the local staging credential is refused on every other bucket (AccessDenied against araripe-cogs and against a new name), no copy tooling exists (grep for copy_object|CopySource|copy_from in src/ and scripts/ returns nothing), and assert_staging_target() would have to be edited — the fail-closed guard that keeps green publication off production, asserted in five places — in the same package that makes the green lane public.
d1_where_the_new_version_lives.the_argument_for_b_that_was_measured_fal: that a public bucket would expose the runs/ prefixes and the probe residue. site/worker/data_route.js never assembles the key from the request: the path after the mount is looked up in an allowlist built from the LIVE release manifest, and the key is release_prefix plus that declared path. runs/, probe prefixes and any non-live release are unreachable by construction, not by filtering.

d5_durable_promotion_history.why_it_is_a_package: it adds a write to atomic_publish.promote and rollback, and that path was proven end to end against real R2 five times on 2026-09-07. Changing it means those proofs no longer cover the code that runs, so it must be built, re-proven, and only then may the retention policy be extended.
d5_durable_promotion_history.why_before_and_not_after: two reasons, the second found 2026-09-27. (1) It blocks nothing and nothing blocks it. (2) Its re-proof is only free BEFORE the cutover: re-proving promote/rollback means moving the green pointer from main, as on 2026-09-07, and that is a sandbox operation only while no public consumer follows the pointer. After the cutover every re-proof would move what the public site shows.
d5_durable_promotion_history.mitigation_considered_and_rejected: requiring a reviewer on the v2-promotion Environment. The stated goal of Package 2B.2C is to keep operational data publication automatic without PRs or manual merges, and a required reviewer on every scheduled publication annuls the package. The mitigation is the history, not the reviewer.
d5_durable_promotion_history.blocks_revocation_detail: corrected 2026-09-27: it never did. The re-proof runs in CI from main with the v2-promotion identity, which the local credential cannot stand in for. See d1_where_the_new_version_lives.revocation_ordering.
